name: Indonesia
summary: No free movement for EU citizens; EU, US and other passports use the same routes. Investors can buy a 5- or 10-year Golden Visa (USD 350,000 in government bonds, or a USD 2.5 million company), or take a Second Home Visa (IDR 2 billion, about USD 130,000, no work). Remote workers (E33G) need about USD 60,000 a year. Retirees need a pension of about USD 3,000 a month. Most official pages could not be opened; figures come from Fragomen, EY, ASEAN Briefing and consultancies.
naturalisation: Citizenship by naturalisation under Law 12/2006 is understood to need age 18+, 5 consecutive years (or 10 non-consecutive) of legal residence, Indonesian language and presidential approval; not confirmed from an official page in this run.
dual_citizenship_note: Indonesia does not allow dual citizenship for adults (limited dual nationality for some children); not verified from an official page in this run.

routes.name: Golden Visa (individual, passive investment route)
routes.summary: Five or ten years of residence for buying Indonesian government bonds worth USD 350,000 to USD 700,000 (secondary sources add listed shares and bank deposits).
routes.requirements: Golden Visa (launched 25 October 2023; first announced 7 September 2023) gives 5 or 10 years of residence with no extra stay or work permits. Individuals: USD 350,000 (5 years) or USD 700,000 (10 years) in Indonesian government bonds; secondary guides also list IDX-listed shares, mutual funds or state-bank deposits and a property route at USD 1 million for 10 years. Not confirmed against the Directorate General of Immigration regulation.
routes.investment_options: USD 350,000 for 5 years; USD 700,000 for 10 years (bonds). Other asset classes per secondary guides, unverified.
routes.family: Spouse and children on dependant stay permits (details not verified).
routes.tax_note: Tax residence follows the 183-day test; a stay permit longer than 183 days may be treated as intent to reside (per a 2026 tax guide, PER-23/PJ/2025, unverified).

routes.name: Golden Visa (individual, own company route)
routes.summary: Five or ten years of residence for an investor who sets up an Indonesian company valued at USD 2.5 million or USD 5 million.
routes.requirements: Golden Visa (launched 25 October 2023; first announced 7 September 2023) gives 5 or 10 years of residence with no extra stay or work permits. Individual company route: establish an Indonesian company with USD 2.5 million (5 years) or USD 5 million (10 years). Corporate route for directors and commissioners: USD 25 million (5 years) or USD 50 million (10 years). Nusantara (IKN) track from 13 January 2026: USD 5 million (5 years) or USD 10 million (10 years), limited to investors linked to listed professional-services firms; Fragomen does not say whether these cut the 2023 figures.
routes.investment_options: USD 5 million for 10 years (individual company); corporate: USD 25 million / USD 50 million.

routes.name: Second Home Visa (Rumah Kedua)
routes.summary: Five or ten years of residence without the right to work, for people who show IDR 2 billion (about USD 130,000) in an Indonesian state bank or own qualifying property.
routes.requirements: Show about IDR 2 billion (USD 130,000) in an individual account at an authorised Indonesian (state-owned per some sources) bank, or property: reports differ (USD 1 million apartment per EY, or Hak Pakai property of IDR 5 billion / apartment of IDR 2 billion per a Bali consultancy). Proof within 90 days or the stay permit is cancelled (secondary). No work allowed. After 3 years may move to a permanent permit (KITAP) per ASEAN Briefing.
routes.investment_options: IDR 2 billion bank balance; or property per conflicting figures.
routes.tax_note: A stay permit over 183 days may make you an Indonesian tax resident.

routes.name: Remote Worker Visa (E33G KITAS)
routes.summary: One-year renewable stay permit for people employed by a foreign company, earning about USD 60,000 a year.
routes.requirements: Contract with a company established outside Indonesia; income about USD 60,000 a year plus about USD 2,000 liquid funds; no work for or payment from Indonesian entities. Validity reported as 1 year renewable (once or more; sources differ). All from consultancy guides; official regulation not opened.
routes.tax_note: Permit over 183 days may count as intent to reside, making you tax resident.

routes.name: Retirement stay permit (E33E Silver Hair / E33F Retirement)
routes.summary: Stay permit for retirees with a pension, no work allowed; one of the few Indonesian long-stay options without an investment.
routes.requirements: Age 55 or 60 depending on the permit and nationality (sources conflict); monthly pension of at least USD 3,000 (undated source); some summaries add a USD 50,000 bank commitment within 90 days; health insurance and accommodation; no work. Permits up to 5 years; may lead to retirement KITAP. Secondary sources only.

routes.name: Work KITAS (RPTKA-sponsored)
routes.summary: Employer-sponsored stay permit (KITAS) for foreign employees; needs a manpower plan (RPTKA) approved for the employer.
routes.requirements: Indonesian sponsor must hold approved RPTKA; foreign worker needs relevant skills, a qualifying position, and an employer-paid skills development fund contribution (USD 100 a month in older rules; not verified). Not researched in detail.
